candidates.title: Introducing MentalHealthBench
candidates.finding: OpenAI describes an open benchmark built from privacy-preserving synthetic conversations with more than 80 licensed mental health experts across 22 countries. Experts write scenario-specific rubric criteria; each conversation is reviewed by at least three experts, and criteria are retained only when at least two agree and a third does not contradict them. Model responses are then graded against the expert-written criteria with an automated grader. A separate user-perspective analysis is reported without changing the benchmark's expert-consensus scoring criteria.
candidates.hilo_adaptation: For HILO development diagnostics, use scenario-specific expert rubrics for difficult human-robot interaction and safety cases, require multi-reviewer agreement before freezing criteria, and keep a separate user-perspective panel rather than silently merging preferences into expert rules. Calibrate any automated grader against held-out human review. This remains a non-ranking diagnostic and cannot replace WANTED retention, consent, or non-compensatory safety gates.

reviewed_not_admitted.title: Offering Zero Data Retention for frontier models — September 22 update
reviewed_not_admitted.reason: The update is relevant privacy architecture and product-policy evidence, but it does not add enough distinct public data-collection or labeling methodology beyond the already staged Privacy Filter and existing purpose-limited access controls to justify a separate worker source card today.
